Subject: Follow-up: budget bands, $/1M token target & runtime batching profile

Thanks for the demo today — helpful walkthrough. Attached is a basic usage spreadsheet so you can see our expected shape. A few clarifying notes from our side: 
- Workload mix: ~70% short chat turns (average 30–50 tokens), 30% longer generations for product descriptions (~500–700 tokens).
- Background jobs: nightly embedding generation for catalog delta (~500 requests/hr) that could be batched.
- Concurrency: customer-facing peak ~120 concurrent sessions, baseline 20–30. We expect peaks for campaigns/holiday spikes.
- Target economics: our finance team is targeting a $/1M-token goal of around $75 but we can stretch a bit for SLA/prod-readiness.

Primary asks: can you confirm if continuous batching on Redwood would meaningfully lower our unit cost given this mix? And what ballpark budget bands should we plan for (monthly) at pilot scale?

Thanks,
Alex Tornek
Director of Product
Spark Commerce

Subject: Re: Follow-up: budget bands, $/1M token target & runtime batching profile

Alex — great to meet you and the team. Short recap and what we recommend as next steps.

Recap of your inputs:
- 70/30 short-chat vs long-gen split, short chats avg ~40 tokens, long gens ~600 tokens.
- Peak concurrency ~120, background embedding jobs ~500/hr.
- Finance target ~$75 / 1M tokens.

Quick answers and assumptions:
- Continuous batching: yes — for your background embedding traffic and longer-generation paths we typically see 3x–5x token compute efficiency with continuous batching and aggressive request coalescing. Short chat turns tend toward lower batching benefit (1.1x–1.5x) because of low token counts but can still benefit from prefix caching and shared KV cache hits.
- Unit economics bands (pilot scale assumptions):
  - Conservative (hosted, no commitment): ~$120–$180 per 1M tokens.
  - Pilot (30–90 days) with batching+cache+modest commitment: ~$45–$75 per 1M tokens (likely achievable given your embedding volume and long-gen mix).
  - Dedicated/reserved with a 6–12 month commit and continuous batching tuned: $30–$50 per 1M tokens.

Key caveats: these ranges assume typical Redwood model variants (open LLMs quantized) and the batching gains depend on real request timing and payload consolidation. We should run a 7–14 day emulation with a subset of production traces to firm numbers.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share an anonymized sample of your request logs (timestamps, token counts, endpoint) — we can use this to simulate batching gains.
2) We run a short sizing pilot on Hosted with batching enabled (2 weeks) and provide a pilot econ sheet.
3) If pilot looks good, discuss Dedicated sizing and commitment bands.

I've attached a quick econ workbook that sketches the math and a sample SOW for a pilot. Available for a follow-up next week — booked a 30m slot here: https://calendar.redwood.ai/rishi/30min

-Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-quick-econ.xlsx (workbook stub)

- Goals: validate unit economics, measure effective $/1M tokens, and confirm latency at 95th %tile under your peak concurrency.
- Success criteria: effective unit cost within agreed band and no more than 200ms median additional latency on short-chat path.
